broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2012 general non-positivity counterexample involves an eight-dimensional nilpotent shift, not a complete irreducible-conservative cycle classification. The eight-state result establishes small-step minimality for arbitrary Markov generators; small-step positivity for n<=7 does not determine an n=4 large-step cutoff. The 2026 Fokker–Planck abstract states results for r(infinity) strictly below 1 or negative; r(infinity)=1 here. Because its full text was not inspected, coverage risk is recorded rather than falsely ruled out.

value.rationale: The exact minimal cyclic state dimension for eventual large-step positivity failure and unique sharp four-cycle cutoff address physically motivated nonnegative Markov propagation for a standard fourth-order rational integrator. The all-n group-inverse expansion identifies a structurally forced first-neighbor negative entry on the critical r(infinity)=1 boundary, rather than a one-off negative numerical example. The result separates conservation and spectral A-stability from entrywise positivity and yields a direct sufficient cycle-specific scaling-and-squaring positivity condition. It does not claim arbitrary-generator optimality or general fourth-order time-step accuracy.
